query_used: Downloaded the 149-page roster PDF; extracted text (pdftotext -layout; surnames letter-spaced UPPERCASE); full-text scan for HUBBELL + variants, then pulled each entry block verbatim.
disambiguation_note: The 153rd roster holds FOUR Hubbells, including TWO named Charles. Surname (or 'Charles') alone is NOT dispositive here — identity required company + hometown + age + fate. The TARGET is Charles F. (Co. I, Champlain, age 25); the two Co. E Minden men are a separate, unrelated Hubbell family; James is the target's younger brother.

candidates.label: TARGET — Charles F. Hubbell

raw_record.verbatim: HUBBELL, CHARLES F.—Age, 25 years. Enlisted, August 30, 1862, at Champlain, to serve three years; mustered in as private, Co. I, October 3, 1862; promoted corporal, October 18, 1862; mustered out with company, October 2, 1865, at Savannah, Ga.

candidates.claude_reasoning: C1 (dispositive in combination): Co. I + the distinctive Champlain enlistment isolate this from the two Co. E (Minden) Hubbells and from brother James. C2: dates inside window; survived war, consistent with post-war death 1875. C4: Champlain hometown. C6: corporal promotion matches the family record. Age 25 in Aug 1862 implies birth c. 1837 — a ~3-year tension with the genealogy's 'b. April 1840' (filed as a discrepancy). Verdict confirmed for IDENTITY; the birth-year question is separate.

candidates.label: BROTHER — James Hubbell (captured here for the James sweep)

raw_record.verbatim: HUBBELL, JAMES.—Age, 22 years. Enlisted in Seventh Congressional District, to serve three years, and mustered in as private, Co. I, March 9, 1864; promoted corporal in May, 186[4]; wounded in action, October 19, 1864, at Cedar Creek, Va.; mustered out with company, October 2, 1865, at Savannah, Ga.

candidates.claude_reasoning: Younger brother; later enlistment (Mar 1864) distinguishes him from Charles (Aug 1862). The 'wounded Oct 19 1864 at Cedar Creek' line matches the family's 'Cedar Creek / night blindness' tradition. NOTE: roster records muster-out 1865, not his death returning home Oct 1865 (post-dates the AG record). Carried into the James sweep.

candidates.label: NOT TARGET — Charles B. Hubbell (different family)

raw_record.verbatim: HUBBELL, CHARLES B.—Age, 44 years. Enlisted, August 30, 1862, at Minden, to serve three years; mustered in as private, Co. E, October 18, 1862; transferred to Veteran Reserve Corps, August 6, 1863, at Washington, D.C.

candidates.claude_reasoning: Wrong company (E), wrong town (Minden, Montgomery Co.), age 44, middle initial B. A separate Hubbell cluster — the classic same-surname false positive the disambiguation rubric exists to catch.

candidates.label: NOT TARGET — J. Elbert / John E. Hubbell (different family)

raw_record.verbatim: HUBBELL, J. ELBERT.—Age, 18 years. Enlisted, August 30, 1862, at Minden... Co. E... wounded in action, October 19, 1864, at Cedar Creek, Va.; promoted corporal, June 1, 1865; mustered out... as John E.

candidates.claude_reasoning: Co. E, Minden — same unrelated family as Charles B. (Note: he too was wounded at Cedar Creek, but in Co. E — a coincidence that underlines why company matters.)

cross_brother_finding: Co. I's ORIGINAL CAPTAIN was Davis J. Rich ('prior service as captain, 34th Infantry') — the same Capt. Davis J. Rich of Henry's Co. D, 34th NY (Henry's 'Capt. Reich', DSC-2026-06-05-002). Henry's company commander later commanded Charles's company. See letter-associates-crossref.json.
notes: No published full-text regimental history of the 153rd exists on archive.org/HathiTrust (the only narrative is the unpublished Enders manuscript at the NY State Library) — so the AG roster is the lone authoritative spine; corroboration shifts to the NYSMM/Phisterer sketch and (handoff) the muster rolls.
